strengths: R2E makes a clear contribution to retrieval-based NLP: candidate-specific masked evidence feeds a compact reasoner, enabling quantitative attribution to the evidence used for prediction. This design is well motivated for biomedical hypothesis prioritization.

The results support the central claim of useful prediction with evidence attribution. On Gene Description Facts, uncorrected R2E improves MRR from the MLM baseline’s 0.167 to 0.202, reaching 0.260 with correction. Clinical AUROC of 0.632 versus MLM’s 0.630 supports the stated performance-parity claim.

Training the encoder from scratch and temporally restricting the literature are sensible contamination controls. Component ablations, experiments incorporating newer evidence without retraining, and comparisons using the same genetics data provide substantive support for the design.

The three released evaluation benchmarks are useful contributions. The appendices document architectures, optimization, dataset construction, prompts, attribution algorithms, and computational costs sufficiently well to support methodological reimplementation.
weaknesses: The explanation evaluation establishes limited alignment with expert judgment. Shapley values attribute scores under the chosen NULL-replacement scheme; interpreting them as scientific evidential strength requires additional validation. Clinical relevance AUROC against GPT-4 is only 0.665, and human validation covers eight hypotheses with one expert. Agreement between GPT-4 and humans does not establish direct agreement between Shapley values and humans. Direct, independently annotated evaluation would strengthen this central contribution.

The clinical benchmark measures a noisy proxy for efficacy. As Appendix P acknowledges, discontinued development can reflect commercial, safety, or molecule-specific failures. Moreover, the genetics evidence from Minikel et al. (2024) is not shown to satisfy the pre-2005 cutoff, and GPT-4 auditing introduces later model knowledge. The literature-only experiment has stronger temporal validity than the multimodal and audited variants; prospective-prediction claims should distinguish these settings.

Some comparative gains are insufficiently isolated. Frequency correction is applied to R2E but not reported for MLM, despite Appendix G explicitly describing its applicability. The GPT-4 comparison uses coarse confidence categories and selected operating points. Clinical improvements over MLM and from auditing are small, and uncertainty across training runs or dependence among hypotheses sharing drugs and genes is not assessed. These limitations reduce confidence in broader superiority claims.

Exact experimental reproduction remains restricted despite the detailed methodological description. The pipeline depends on proprietary entity linking and a partly licensed literature corpus, while training code and model weights are explicitly withheld. A reference implementation and an experiment using an accessible corpus would substantially improve independent verification.

The theoretical justification in Appendices F–G needs correction. Section 3.4 excludes the true entity when sampling negatives, so the negative distribution is not independent of the query as assumed in the derivation. Writing p = P(a|q,L=1), the stated sampler gives P(a|q,L=0) = (1-p)/(|A|-1), yielding optimal logit log((|A|-1)p/(1-p)). This preserves uncorrected ranking monotonicity, but the claimed log-probability and PMI relationships require an explicit approximation or revised derivation.
